thread:
sara: Customer reports audit-log delivery lag (~30-40m) from their Private VPC deployment + intermittent KMS 403s when we push to their SIEM. Started after customer deployed NAT changes around 03:10 UTC. Any initial thoughts?

jamal: Can you share sample event timestamps and any gateway logs?

sara: tenant=acme-inc, sample event produced 2026-03-16T03:25:12Z, arrived at our collector 2026-03-16T03:55:40Z. Gateway logs show a few "kms:AccessDenied" entries around 03:28.

eli: That smells like NAT/conntrack idle timeouts with pooled keepalive connections getting dropped mid-use. If our agent reuses a TCP/TLS connection and the NAT drops state, the next packet might get blackholed or cause a half-handshake and KMS to respond oddly.

mike: Are these long-lived connections from the audit agent? Normally KMS calls are short but if there is batching they can be held open. Could a firewall middlebox be tearing state? :thinking:

sara: Customer uses a customer-managed NAT instance + stateful egress firewall (default-deny, allowlist to *.kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com). They recently changed NAT software version.

jamal: Triage checklist to reproduce / confirm:
1) tcpdump on customer NAT and on our control-plane egress around the event window to look for RST/FIN/ICMP
2) conntrack dump from NAT: `sudo conntrack -L | grep <agent-ip>`
3) kube-proxy / node conntrack metrics (conntrack_count, failed lookups)
4) curl test with verbose TLS from a node behind the NAT:
```
curl -v --resolve kms.acme:443:10.0.2.5 https://kms.acme/health
```
5) check our audit-agent batching/retry configuration and backlog metrics (if it queued logs for 30m due to transient egress failure)

sara: I asked the customer for tcpdump + conntrack. Anything quick we can check from CP without their pcap?

eli: From control plane, check: ENI metrics (Tx/Rx drops), edge-proxy logs for 403s with SNI/ALPN details, and our gateway TLS handshake logs to see client hello vs server hello timings. Also verify that the KMS hostname in SNI exactly matches their firewall allowlist entry.

mike: FYI AWS NAT Gateway idle timeout is ~350s; on customer-managed NAT instances conntrack timeouts can be much shorter depending on kernel config. If the NAT drops conntrack while a connection is idle, an in-flight keepalive could be dropped.

jamal: If conntrack expires while our agent thinks connection is established, packets may not match an existing state and be dropped; client will often retry and that can trigger KMS side rate-limiting or auth anomalies. Key artifacts: conntrack timestamps aligned to TCP FIN/RST in pcap.

sara: Customer uploaded pcap. I see a SYN->SYN/ACK then an ACK, and ~5 minutes later a FIN/RST emitted by the NAT. Snippet: 
```
03:25:10.123 IP agent>kms TLSv1.2 Handshake
03:30:12.456 IP agent>kms RST
```

eli: That FIN/RST after ~5m points to a short conntrack timeout. Ask them to temporarily increase conntrack timeout and enable TCP keepalives on the audit-agent (or application-level pings). Also recommend switching to stateless short-lived requests or explicit idempotent retries for delivery so broken connections don't cause long delays.

sara: They've bumped conntrack to 20m and enabled TCP keepalive. Re-running ingestion now.

infra-bot: deploy 2141239001 initiated by jamal (eng-infra): rolling restart of audit-agent with keepalive=30s

mike: Also confirm there isn't asymmetric routing or a stateful firewall in front that rewrites seq/ack causing connection confusion. Those middleboxes are nasty.

sara: After the change, new audit events are delivered in ~2 minutes. They still saw a single KMS 403 at 03:48 but no continuous failures.

eli: For long-term mitigations:
- Default keepalive in audit-agent config
- Queue/backlog metric and paging threshold if backlog > 5m
- Runbook entry: check KMS allowlist vs SNI, conntrack, NAT idleness, and request idempotency

jamal: Action items:
- sara: attach pcap + conntrack dump to support ticket (in progress)
- jamal: push audit-agent patch to enable keepalive by default and add backlog alert
- eli: update eng-security runbook with KMS+conntrack troubleshooting steps and hostnames to validate in SNI/ALPN

security-bot: incident-classification: low-sev (customer partial degradation), tags: kms, vpc, conntrack, audit-logs

sara: Thanks all :heart: I'll close once ticket and artifacts are in the case.
